extracted.subtask_description: A news report about CNET publishing AI-written stories that contained errors and plagiarism, the internal review and corrections, and the publisher's response on disclosure and use of AI. Useful for understanding standards and failures around AI-generated journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: "We are currently reviewing the story for accuracy. We will correct any errors found and update the story." (page reports an internal review revealed many errors.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should be reviewed for factual correctness; CNET corrected 41 of 77 AI-written stories after errors were found. Accuracy reviews should trigger corrections and updates when problems are identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / Plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: The article states the internal review "revealed many errors and plagiarism" and notes correction notes such as "We’ve replaced phrases that were not entirely original."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content must be original; any non-original phrasing discovered should be replaced and disclosed in correction notes. Examples cited include multiple AI-written pieces that contained unoriginal language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of AI use
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclaimer was added to all AI-written stories following the errors; the piece also reports CNET "had published articles in AI for months without making any formal announcement."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers should disclose when articles are AI-generated or substantially assisted by AI (e.g., visible disclaimer). Lack of disclosure is framed as a problem that prompted company action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction and update policy
rubrics_metrics.description: CNET corrected 41 of the 77 stories it published that were created using an AI tool and added a disclaimer; the public-facing note promises to "correct any errors found and update the story."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a clear process for issuing corrections and updating affected stories promptly; corrections and disclaimers should be posted where readers will see them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human oversight and authorship transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece reports that "the staff often didn’t know whether a machine or a human coworker wrote the content."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial processes should ensure staff know authorship (human vs. machine) and provide sufficient human oversight of AI-produced drafts to catch errors and originality issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using AI to manipulate search/SEO
rubrics_metrics.description: The article states these AI-written articles "aim to manipulate Google searches using SEO-friendly keywords."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using AI primarily to game search rankings (SEO-first publication) is presented negatively; editorial standards should prioritize journalistic quality over traffic manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible experimentation with AI
rubrics_metrics.description: CNET leadership said they would "continue to explore and test AI to assist our teams in their work. We will embrace it and any new technology that improves our lives."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers may test AI tools as assistive technology, but experimentation should be paired with accuracy checks, disclosure, and safeguards to prevent plagiarism and errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial transparency / conflict-of-interest awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: The article notes parent company Red Ventures "can reap the benefits when a reader registers for a credit account from one of these highly-trafficked articles."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When content strategies (including AI use) are tied to monetization, outlets should be mindful of and disclose commercial incentives to avoid eroding trust or prioritizing revenue over editorial standards.
